2. Abyākaraṇīyapañha 2. Question on What Is Not to Be Answered

“Bhante nāgasena, bhāsitampetaṁ bhagavatā—“Venerable Nāgasena, this too was said by the Blessed One: ‘natthānanda, tathāgatassa dhammesu ācariyamuṭṭhī’ti, puna ca therena mālukyaputtena pañhaṁ puṭṭho na byākāsi. ‘Ānanda, the Tathāgata has no closed fist of a teacher with regard to the teachings.’ And yet when the elder Māluṅkyaputta put a question to him, he did not answer. Eso kho, bhante nāgasena, pañho dvayanto ekantanissito bhavissati ajānanena vā guyhakaraṇena vā. This question, Venerable Nāgasena, will be one-sided on either horn: either it was through not knowing, or through concealing it. Yadi, bhante nāgasena, bhagavatā bhaṇitaṁ—If, Venerable Nāgasena, the Blessed One said ‘natthānanda, tathāgatassa dhammesu ācariyamuṭṭhī’ti, tena hi therassa mālukyaputtassa ajānantena na byākataṁ. ‘The Tathāgata has no closed fist of a teacher with regard to the teachings,’ then he did not answer the elder Māluṅkyaputta because he did not know. Yadi jānantena na byākataṁ, tena hi atthi tathāgatassa dhammesu ācariyamuṭṭhi. But if he did not answer while knowing, then the Tathāgata does have a closed fist of a teacher with regard to the teachings. Ayampi ubhato koṭiko pañho tavānuppatto, so tayā nibbāhitabbo”ti. This too is a two-horned dilemma that has been put to you for you to resolve.”

“Bhāsitampetaṁ, mahārāja, bhagavatā ‘natthānanda, tathāgatassa dhammesu ācariyamuṭṭhī’ti, abyākato ca therena mālukyaputtena pucchito pañho, tañca pana na ajānantena na guyhakaraṇena. “Your majesty, the Blessed One did say ‘Ānanda, the Tathāgata has no closed fist of a teacher with regard to the teachings,’ and the question put by the elder Māluṅkyaputta did go unanswered. But that was neither through not knowing nor through concealing it. Cattārimāni, mahārāja, pañhabyākaraṇāni. There are four ways of answering a question, your majesty. Katamāni cattāri? What are the four? Ekaṁsabyākaraṇīyo pañho vibhajjabyākaraṇīyo pañho paṭipucchābyākaraṇīyo pañho ṭhapanīyo pañhoti. A question to be answered categorically; a question to be answered by analysis; a question to be answered by counter-questioning; and a question to be set aside.

Katamo ca, mahārāja, ekaṁsabyākaraṇīyo pañho? And what, your majesty, is a question to be answered categorically? ‘Rūpaṁ aniccan’ti ekaṁsabyākaraṇīyo pañho, ‘Is form impermanent’: this is a question to be answered categorically. ‘vedanā aniccā’ti …pe… ‘Is feeling impermanent’... ‘saññā aniccā’ti …pe… ‘Is perception impermanent’... ‘saṅkhārā aniccā’ti …pe… ‘Are formations impermanent’... ‘viññāṇaṁ aniccan’ti ekaṁsabyākaraṇīyo pañho, ayaṁ ekaṁsabyākaraṇīyo pañho. ‘Is consciousness impermanent’: this is a question to be answered categorically. These are questions to be answered categorically.

Katamo vibhajjabyākaraṇīyo pañho? What is a question to be answered by analysis? ‘Aniccaṁ pana rūpan’ti vibhajjabyākaraṇīyo pañho, ‘Is form, thus, impermanent?’ is a question to be answered by analysis. ‘aniccā pana vedanā’ti …pe… ‘Is feeling, thus, impermanent?’... ‘aniccā pana saññā’ti …pe… ‘Is perception, thus, impermanent?’... ‘aniccā pana saṅkhārā’ti …pe… ‘Are formations, thus, impermanent?’... ‘aniccaṁ pana viññāṇan’ti vibhajjabyākaraṇīyo pañho, ayaṁ vibhajjabyākaraṇīyo pañho. ‘Is consciousness, thus, impermanent?’: this is a question to be answered by analysis. These are questions to be answered by analysis.

Katamo paṭipucchābyākaraṇīyo pañho? What is a question to be answered by counter-questioning? ‘Kiṁ nu kho cakkhunā sabbaṁ vijānātī’ti ayaṁ paṭipucchābyākaraṇīyo pañho. ‘Does one cognize everything with the eye?’ This is a question to be answered by counter-questioning.

Katamo ṭhapanīyo pañho? What is a question to be set aside? ‘Sassato loko’ti ṭhapanīyo pañho, ‘Is the world eternal’; ‘asassato loko’ti, ‘is the world not eternal’; ‘antavā loko’ti, ‘is the world finite’; ‘anantavā loko’ti, ‘is the world infinite’; ‘antavā ca anantavā ca loko’ti, ‘is the world both finite and infinite’; ‘nevantavā nānantavā loko’ti, ‘is the world neither finite nor infinite’; ‘taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīran’ti, ‘are the soul and the body the same’; ‘aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīran’ti, ‘is the soul one thing and the body another’; ‘hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti, ‘does the Tathāgata exist after death’; ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti, ‘does the Tathāgata not exist after death’; ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti, ‘does the Tathāgata both exist and not exist after death’; ‘neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṁ maraṇā’ti ṭhapanīyo pañho, ‘does the Tathāgata neither exist nor not exist after death’: this is a question to be set aside. ayaṁ ṭhapanīyo pañho. These are questions to be set aside.

Bhagavā, mahārāja, therassa mālukyaputtassa taṁ ṭhapanīyaṁ pañhaṁ na byākāsi. The Blessed One, your majesty, did not answer the elder Māluṅkyaputta’s question because it was one to be set aside. So pana pañho kiṅkāraṇā ṭhapanīyo? And why should that question be set aside? Na tassa dīpanāya hetu vā kāraṇaṁ vā atthi, tasmā so pañho ṭhapanīyo. There is no cause or reason that would serve to explain it; therefore it is to be set aside. Natthi buddhānaṁ bhagavantānaṁ akāraṇamahetukaṁ giramudīraṇan”ti. For the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, there is no uttering of speech without cause and without reason.” “Sādhu, bhante nāgasena, evametaṁ tathā sampaṭicchāmī”ti. “Well said, Venerable Nāgasena. I accept it as you say.”

Abyākaraṇīyapañho dutiyo. Question on What Is Not to Be Answered second
